modules.name: web-presentation-pages
owns: Three-state rendering: explicit `loading` boolean (decoupled from data nullability), empty state (balances.length === 0 → explicit 'no balances yet' message), error state (role="alert")
Full per-leave-type balance breakdown rendering: entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays, available, with period dates via formatUtcDate

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — DashboardPage rendering: full breakdown, empty state, decoupled loading
recommended_phases.rationale: Single-file change to DashboardPage.tsx. Add an explicit `loading` boolean state (set false in both then and catch) so a balances-only failure surfaces the error state, never a permanent loading page. Render entitled/used/pending/available per leave type using the already-fetched LeaveBalanceView fields and formatUtcDate. Add an explicit empty state when balances.length === 0, visually distinct from loading and error.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — DashboardPage tests: empty case, balances-fetch error, full breakdown
recommended_phases.rationale: Extend DashboardPage.test.tsx beside the subject. Cover the empty-balances case (explicit empty message, not an empty list), a balances-fetch rejection (error state, not loading), and the full breakdown rendering (entitled/used/pending/available values visible).

app_notes: This is a narrow web/ presentation-layer change confined to DashboardPage.tsx and its test. No new service interfaces, repositories, or shared types are required: `IBalanceService.getBalances()` already returns `LeaveBalanceView[]` carrying `entitledDays`, `usedDays`, `pendingDays`, and `available` (all fetched, currently discarded), and `formatUtcDate` already handles Date|string. The only production change is DashboardPage rendering: (1) render the full per-leave-type breakdown (entitled/used/pending/available) with period dates; (2) add an explicit empty state when `balances.length === 0`; (3) introduce an explicit `loading` boolean set false in both the `.then` and `.catch` branches so a balances-only failure surfaces the error state rather than a permanently loading page. The three states (loading / empty / error) are rendered distinctly. No backend, API contract, route, or page changes. Dependency direction is preserved: presentation -> modules -> infrastructure -> shared, with no new edges beyond the existing web-presentation-pages -> {web-shared-types, web-shared-date, web-leave, web-employee, web-auth, web-presentation-components}.
auth_contract: No new API surface or role-gated access is introduced by this feature; the dashboard is already behind the existing authenticated session. authContract is intentionally empty.
error_response_contract: No new endpoints are introduced; the existing GET /balances/me and api-client.getBalances are unchanged. errorResponseContract is intentionally empty.
